constraints.title: A required closing-packet artifact went unwritten in two consecutive runs, unnoticed by runs and operator alike
constraints.statement: RESEARCH-BACKLOG-v1.json absent from RUN-20260807-5 and RUN-20260807-6: never created (git log --all: zero commits touch either path), never named in any of their files. Sizes across the program: 13,684 / 8,714 / 6,180 / 6,876 / 0 / 0 bytes. Both runs declared clean final trees; the operator's verification of RUN-5's packet also missed it. Completed by this run as labelled post-hoc reconstructions from committed artifacts -- a weaker source than live reasoning, said so in each file.

evidence.verification: this run's opening commit: presence/size table and git-log-all counts, matching the owner's figures exactly

constraints.cause: See BRF-101 -- instruction decay, evidenced, not the 'no natural trigger' speculation this run's brief initially carried.
constraints.remediation: Both files written with postHocCompletion headers and causeCorrection fields; tests/test_closing_packets.py permanently fails any close missing or emptying a required artifact (side 1 of the M26 fix). It also rejects EMPTY required artifacts: this run's own opening commit briefly carried PROMPT.txt as an empty placeholder -- the defect class's smallest specimen, caught and recorded in the capture note.
constraints.affectsConclusionsReason: The backlog carries forward learning; no scientific number lived in the missing files. What was at risk was un-acted-on knowledge (the SCH-001 elevation, the mapping-pipeline surface) existing nowhere.

constraints.title: The evidenced cause: operator briefs replaced the packet enumeration with a concept, and output tracked instruction exactly (owner's own finding)
constraints.statement: Only RUN-1's brief enumerates the closing packet by member name. RUN-4/5/6's briefs say only 'Close with the full versioned packet'; the string RESEARCH-BACKLOG appears in none of them (verified by grep, with one refinement to the owner's table: RUN-2/3's briefs also never name it -- those runs produced backlogs from the enumeration still fresh in context as precedent). RUN-5/6, concept-only briefs with the precedent aged out, never attempted the artifact. The M24 defect -- concepts are not quantifiers -- one layer up, in the instruction layer, identified and evidenced by the owner against the owner's own briefs.

evidence.grep: RESEARCH-BACKLOG occurrences per brief: RUN-1: 1; RUN-2..6: 0. 'full [versioned] packet' present in RUN-2/4/5/6 briefs
evidence.outcome: artifact present 4/4 while enumeration or fresh precedent was in context; absent 2/2 once neither was

constraints.requirement: STATED AS A REQUIREMENT ON OPERATOR BRIEFS, per owner instruction, not as advice: a brief that requires a packet ENUMERATES its members or cites the enumeration of record (tests/test_closing_packets.py::REQUIRED) by path. A future brief that says 'the full packet' without naming the members is DEFECTIVE, and the run receiving it says so before executing -- the same standing a defective registration has.
constraints.whyItGeneralises: Three layers in one day named a concept where members belonged and failed at the unnamed members: an expectation (REG-101's E4), a specification (SPEC-108's unregistered receipt object), an instruction (this). The instruction layer is the one that actually caused this loss, and the only one that had no check until now.
constraints.discoveredDuring: owner correction, mid-RUN-20260807-7; verified by grep before adoption
constraints.status: recorded; requirement standing; enforcement side in tests/test_closing_packets.py

constraints.title: Prompt capture is agent-transcription for the seventh consecutive run; this run adds a mid-run correction message as a second transcribed input
constraints.statement: PROMPT.txt and PROMPT-CORRECTION.txt both agent-transcribed, unverified (PROV-004..012 line). Additionally the opening commit carried PROMPT.txt as an empty placeholder, corrected in the same run and recorded in the capture note.
